input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign: vLLM serving functional and performance parity

## Description

This investigation resolves the central unknown of the AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement strategy: whether vLLM serving on AMD Instinct accelerators reaches functional and performance parity with the platform's CUDA builds for the supported model set. It runs a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware and produces the parity report and per-model go/no-go scope that determines which models the productized ROCm serving runtime will support. The campaign's outcome gates the downstream productization work: a model that clears becomes supported; a model that fails is excluded (or, on a full no-go, productization does not proceed).

## Scope

- Stand up the validation environment on dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (securing procurement or partner-lab access is part of this epic's work; the access itself is an externally-granted precondition tracked in Risks).
- Run vLLM serving for every model in the supported model set using upstream ROCm runtime images, exercising the platform's serving path end to end (models served through KServe InferenceServices, which require no code change for a ROCm runtime image).
- Record functional results per model: correct loading, inference correctness, and error behavior on ROCm versus the CUDA baseline.
- Record performance parity data per model: throughput and latency against the CUDA baseline on comparable hardware.
- Define and apply the pass/fail criteria for functional correctness and performance parity thresholds.
- Produce the campaign report: per-model results, the go/no-go scope for productization, and the exact ROCm image digests validated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The campaign report covers every model in the supported model set with an explicit functional pass/fail result for vLLM serving on ROCm.
- The campaign report records performance parity data (throughput and latency versus the CUDA baseline) for every model in the supported model set.
- The campaign report documents the go/no-go scope for productization: the list of models cleared for the supported ROCm serving runtime, with the decision criteria applied.
- The campaign report records the exact ROCm runtime image digests used for the validated results.
- Serving during the campaign is exercised through KServe InferenceServices on AMD Instinct nodes (KServe kept working, no code change).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware access is an availability precondition granted by parties outside this strategy (procurement or partner lab); it is unresolved at decomposition time and is not controlled by this epic's engineering work. If access is delayed, the campaign schedule slips accordingly — this is a program-level risk, not a deliverable condition.
- Upstream ROCm runtime image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities; the campaign pins the image digests it validates and is therefore insensitive to later upstream releases, but a mid-campaign upstream breaking change would require re-validation.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for validated models

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models cleared by the validation campaign, closing the gap that the platform today ships only CUDA runtime builds. It delivers the productized ROCm build of the vLLM runtime (built and released per platform version from the midstream), pins the campaign-validated ROCm image digests, and declares support only for the cleared model set.

## Scope

- Build the vLLM ROCm runtime image from the midstream for AMD Instinct accelerators, following the existing runtime build and release process used for the CUDA builds.
- Pin the ROCm base image digests that the validation campaign cleared.
- Declare the supported model list as exactly the models the campaign cleared; models that did not clear are explicitly not supported.
- Provide the ServingRuntime support so the ROCm vLLM runtime serves the cleared models under KServe InferenceServices on AMD Instinct nodes (KServe itself requires no code change).
- Ensure runtime image builds are green in the existing build pipeline (the component is already build-pipeline onboarded).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A vLLM ROCm serving runtime image is built from the midstream and released per platform version, with builds green in the existing build pipeline.
- The runtime pins the exact ROCm image digests validated by the campaign (recorded in the campaign report).
- The supported model list for the ROCm runtime equals the go/no-go scope produced by the validation campaign — no model is marked supported that the campaign did not clear.
- Each cleared model serves successfully through a KServe InferenceService using the productized ROCm runtime on AMD Instinct nodes.
- The runtime is documented as supported for AMD Instinct accelerators in the component's support statement.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks / Notes

- Scope is gated on the validation campaign's outcome: the epic is rewritten (narrowed) to the cleared model set; a full no-go removes the epic.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and may not align with platform release trains; the pinned-digest approach trades currency for the validated parity data (the shipped ROCm base may be older than upstream latest).

# PyTorch ROCm training support for single- and multi-GPU jobs

## Description

This epic makes PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) a supported capability of the Training Operator: single-GPU and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs run to completion on AMD GPU nodes and are admitted through Kueue, including jobs requesting the amd.com/gpu resource. It delivers the job/runtime support for ROCm training and validates the capability on physical AMD Instinct hardware.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob execution on AMD Instinct nodes for ROCm: worker pod configuration for AMD GPU nodes (runtime images, node affinity, and any operator-side support needed for ROCm-based workers).
- Support single-GPU and multi-GPU (multi-replica) PyTorchJob topologies on ROCm.
- Validate that PyTorchJobs requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted through Kueue and run to completion, using the Kueue quota handling for AMD GPU resources.
- Record validation results on physical AMD Instinct hardware (securing node access is part of this epic's work; the access itself is an externally-granted precondition tracked in Risks).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using ROCm on an AMD Instinct node runs to completion with correct training results.
- A multi-GPU (multi-replica) PyTorchJob using ROCm across multiple AMD Instinct GPUs runs to completion with correct training results.
- PyTorchJobs requesting the amd.com/gpu resource are admitted through Kueue (workload queueing enabled) and run under the amd.com/gpu quota configuration.
- The validation results on physical AMD Instinct hardware are recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, partial): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — this epic covers the Training Operator side (job and runtime support, end-to-end training validation).

## Risks / Notes

- Requires the Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for AMD Instinct nodes to be in place for the admission-related acceptance criteria; that work proceeds in the Distributed Workloads component and is tracked as a dependency.
- Hardware access: validation requires dedicated AMD Instinct nodes not present in the CI fleet; procurement or partner-lab access is an externally-granted precondition and may slip the validation schedule.
- Upstream PyTorch/ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities; validation pins the image digests it exercises.
- Shared-hardware coordination: serving validation for this strategy consumes the same scarce AMD Instinct nodes; plan node scheduling across the two validation efforts.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for AMD Instinct nodes

## Description

This epic delivers amd.com/gpu quota handling in the Distributed Workloads (Kueue) queueing layer so that jobs requesting AMD Instinct GPUs are admitted, quota-accounted, and gang-scheduled correctly. It extends the existing ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model — currently exercised for NVIDIA GPU resources — to the amd.com/gpu resource on AMD GPU nodes, enabling PyTorch training (and other queued workloads) to be admitted through Kueue with AMD GPU quota.

## Scope

- Define the AMD GPU resource flavor and quota configuration for amd.com/gpu within the Kueue quota model (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue), covering AMD Instinct node pools.
- Ensure quota accounting and all-or-nothing (gang) admission semantics work for workloads requesting amd.com/gpu, including multi-GPU job topologies that must be admitted atomically.
- Cover the integration with the Training Operator's PyTorchJob admission path (workload admission via kueue.x-k8s.io labels/queues).
- Validate quota behavior on (or representative of) AMD Instinct node pools: admission within quota, denial over quota, and pending workloads reported per queue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Kueue quota configuration handles the amd.com/gpu resource: workloads requesting amd.com/gpu are admitted when quota is available and denied (left pending) when quota is exhausted.
- All-or-nothing admission is preserved for multi-GPU jobs requesting amd.com/gpu: a job is admitted only when all its GPUs can be accounted for.
- PyTorchJobs submitted through the Training Operator with kueue.x-k8s.io queue labels are admitted through a ClusterQueue/LocalQueue carrying amd.com/gpu quota.
- Quota behavior is validated with recorded results.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, partial): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — this epic covers the Distributed Workloads side (Kueue quota and admission handling for the amd.com/gpu resource).

## Risks / Notes

- Full end-to-end validation against physical AMD Instinct nodes depends on the same externally-granted hardware access as the rest of the strategy; quota semantics can be validated on representative node pools in the interim.
- Out of scope per the strategy: AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support (no time-slicing equivalent for amd.com/gpu is attempted).

# Document supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and validated model list

## Description

This epic authors the customer-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement: what AMD hardware is supported, which driver prerequisites must be in place on the cluster, and which models are validated for the supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime and for PyTorch training on ROCm. It is the documentation work stream of the strategy and runs after the implementation work so the docs describe what was actually built and validated.

## Scope

- New documentation topics covering:
  - Supported AMD hardware (Instinct accelerators and node requirements) for serving and training.
  - Driver and platform prerequisites for ROCm workloads (GPU driver expectations on AMD Instinct nodes).
  - The validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, sourced from the validation campaign's go/no-go scope and the productized runtime's supported model statement.
  - PyTorch training on ROCm: single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs admitted through Kueue, including amd.com/gpu quota configuration guidance.
  - Any known limitations recorded by the validation campaign (models that did not clear, parity caveats).
- Follow the Red Hat docs content process for authoring, building, and publishing these topics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the supported AMD hardware for both serving (vLLM ROCm runtime) and training (PyTorch on ROCm).
- Published documentation states the driver prerequisites for AMD Instinct nodes running ROCm workloads.
- Published documentation states the validated model list, matching the productized ROCm serving runtime's supported model list exactly.
- Published documentation covers PyTorch ROCm training configuration, including Kueue admission with amd.com/gpu quota.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented and validated capabilities (serving runtime, training support, and quota handling) before publication.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list.

## Risks / Notes

- The validated model list is only as final as the validation campaign's outcome; if the campaign no-goes, this epic documents the negative result and the supported-hardware statement changes accordingly.
- Priority note: this epic's priority derives from the strategy's overall priority (Major → P1) per the docs-authoring priority exception, not from HLR-4's P2 label; it does not push priority onto any implementation work.
